overview.body:
**Tagaloa** ​(*tagaloa*) ‌— ‌Creator, Ocean ​· ​The ​lord ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Polynesian ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Creator, Ocean". ​The ​name ​means ‌"The ​lord".

**Tagaloa** ‌is ​creator, ‌ocean. ​The ‌name means ​"The ‌lord" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the polynesian ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Tagaloa** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/tagaloa/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*tagaloa* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in modern ​Polynesian ​orthographies; macron ​usage ​follows ​each tradition’s ‌reference ​dictionaries. Etymologically ​the ‌name means ​"The ‌lord".

The ​ASCII ‌form *tagaloa* ​survives ​only because ​the ​early domain-name ​system ‌could ​not carry ‌diacritics; ​it is ‌a ​technological compromise, ‌not ​an ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ​restoration ‌**Tagaloa** recovers ‌the ‌full diacritic ​detail ​of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly in ‌the ​address bar. ​The ‌restoration needs ​no ‌distinctive letters ​or ​diacritics its ​ASCII ​form would ‌lose, ‌which ​places the ‌name ​in Tier ​2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ‌**t** ​→ **T** ‌— ​Same, capitalized
​- ​**a** → ‌**a** ​— ​Same
- ​**g** ‌→ **g** ​— ​Same
- ​**a** ‌→ **a** ​— ‌Same
- ​**l** ‌→ **l** ​— ‌Same
- ‌**o** ​→ ​**o** — ​Same
​- **a** ‌→ ‌**a** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/tagaloa/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**tagaloa** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Tagaloa.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"tagaloa" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Tagaloa".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"tagaloa" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Tagaloa" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Tagaloa was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Tagaloa ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Tagaloa ‌place ​creator, ocean ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Tagaloa ‌appears ​in polynesian ‌tradition ​as ​creator, ocean. ​The ​name's ​meaning, "The ‌lord", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Tagaloa ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Tagaloa ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Tagaloa ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Tagaloa ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Polynesian ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Tagaloa, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​creator ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Tagaloa ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​creator, Ocean ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"The ​lord" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​creator, ‌Ocean ​· ​The ‌lord.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Tagaloa ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *tagaloa* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
